title: Every text went to the same customer

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the demo schedules Saturday's reminders with real timers and prints each text.

tasks.title: Catch the texts all going to one person
tasks.description:
Before you change anything, capture the bug without waiting on real timers. In `src/reproduce.js`, implement `reproduceSameReminder()`.

Call the original `scheduleReminders(saturday, send, setTimer)` with:

- a `send(to, text)` that pushes `{ to, text }` into an array
- a fake `setTimer(callback, ms)` that only saves `callback`

After `scheduleReminders` returns, call every saved callback, then return the array of `{ to, text }`. The check runs your function against the original `reminders.js`.
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.js` and read who each text goes to.
Write a `send` and a fake `setTimer` that push into two arrays.
Pass both to `scheduleReminders`, then call every saved callback.
Return the texts and run the demo again.
hints: A fake timer is just a function with the same arguments as `setTimeout` that stores the callback instead of scheduling it.
Running the saved callbacks after the loop is exactly what real timers do: they fire when the loop is long gone.
You should get three entries, and all three go to Priya at +44 7700 900303.

tasks.title: One customer, one text
tasks.description:
Fix `scheduleReminders(bookings, send, setTimer = setTimeout)` in `src/reminders.js`.

- For each booking, call `setTimer(callback, booking.remindInMs)` once.
- When that callback runs, it calls `send(booking.phone, text)` with that booking's text: `Hi ${name}, your ${boat} is ready at ${time}.`
- Nothing is sent before its timer fires.
- The caller may empty or reuse its `bookings` array right after scheduling, and the texts must still be right.
- Return the number of reminders scheduled.

The check drives your function with a fake timer and with real timers.
nextSteps: Find which variable every callback reads when it finally runs.
Give each pass of the loop its own binding for the booking.
Keep the callback a function that sends later, not a call that sends now.
Run `node src/demo.js` and check each text.
hints: `var` belongs to the whole function, not to one pass of the loop. There is only one `booking` variable, and all three callbacks share it.
`let` and `const` inside a loop body make a fresh binding on every pass, so each callback can close over its own one.
Changing the loop counter to `let` is not enough while `booking` is still a `var`. Declare the booking itself with `const`, or loop with `for...of`.

tasks.title: Write the test that would have caught it
tasks.description:
Write vitest tests in `src/reminders.test.js` with your own fake `setTimer` that saves each callback and delay. They should check that:

- nothing is sent while the reminders are being scheduled
- once you run the saved callbacks, each customer got a text about their own booking

The check runs your test file three times: beside the original `reminders.js` (it must fail), beside a correct fix (it must pass) and beside a fix that builds each text correctly but sends it right away instead of when the timer fires (it must fail).
nextSteps: Write a helper that calls `scheduleReminders` with a fake `send` and `setTimer`.
Assert what was sent before you run any saved callback.
Run the callbacks and assert every `{ to, text }` exactly.
hints: Real timers make tests slow and flaky. A fake one gives you control over when the callbacks run.
The wrong fix passes `send(...)` to `setTimer`, so `send` runs immediately and `setTimer` gets `undefined`.
Check `sent` is empty right after scheduling, and only then run the callbacks and check the three texts.
